title: The Well of the Ninth Floor
premise: Zephyrine Marchetti inherits his estranged family's ancestral house in the village of Vellacourt, a place where the dying have always heard a bell toll and counted backwards from nine. He dismisses it as hospice-trained suggestion until the melted bell of 1911 rings again, and the counting spreads from the deathbeds to the healthy. The Marchettis have survived nine generations by feeding the Well beneath the ninth floor one member per generation; Zephyrine, the one who left and was never chosen, must break the covenant before the Well finishes counting down to his daughter, or seal it forever by giving it what it has always wanted: the one who got away.
about_author: Sebastian Marchetti is the pen name of a former night-shift caregiver who spent eleven years in palliative wards across northern France and claims to have heard the counting exactly once. He writes in a locked room on the top floor of his house and refuses, on principle, to own a bell of any kind.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He arrives in Vellacourt with his teenage daughter Odile to claim a house he's never seen, left by a grandmother he never met. The solicitor's hands shake as he hands over the keys. Emotional beat: wary detachment masking grief he hasn't processed since his wife's death.

chapters.title: Ninth Floor, Sealed
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The house has eight floors and a bricked-up stairwell to a ninth. Odile hears humming through the bricks; Zephyrine hears nothing and tells himself that's reassuring. Emotional beat: the first hairline crack in his skepticism.

chapters.title: The Village That Doesn't Greet
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. At the tavern he learns the Marchettis are spoken of only in past tense, though the family is standing right in front of the locals. An old woman presses a wax earplug into Odile's hand. Emotional beat: the chill of being known and unwelcomed at once.

chapters.title: What the Dying Count
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The village's last hospice patient grabs his wrist and counts backwards from nine, in his grandmother's voice, then dies smiling. Zephyrine recognizes the voice and cannot explain how. Emotional beat: professional calm curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Bell of 1911
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. At midnight the church bell rings, though the parish records confirm it was melted for the war effort a century ago. Every villager stands in the street, silent, counting. Emotional beat: the moment denial stops being an available comfort.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Exploring the attic, Odile finds a ledger listing nine Marchetti names per century, each with a death date and the word 'paid.' The final page lists Zephyrine's name, uncrossed, and beneath it, freshly inked: hers. Emotional beat: a child's loyalty turning to fear for her father.

chapters.title: The Cousin Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A gaunt man named Ambrose Marchetti appears, claiming to be a cousin who never left. He explains the covenant: the Well beneath the ninth floor keeps the village alive, fed one Marchetti per generation. Emotional beat: the horror of learning survival was always a transaction.

chapters.title: Nine Floors Down
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Ambrose unbricks the stairwell. The ninth floor is a single room with a well shaft descending beyond sight, and the air tastes of coins and riverbed. Something below exhales. Emotional beat: vertigo, both physical and moral.

chapters.title: Odile Hears It First
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile begins counting in her sleep. Zephyrine wakes to find her standing at the sealed stairwell, fingers moving like a metronome. She doesn't remember. Emotional beat: a father's terror weaponized against his rationalism.

chapters.title: The Village's Quiet Bargain
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The villagers are healthy, long-lived, and complicit. The tavern keeper explains, gently, that everyone in Vellacourt lives on Marchetti time. They will not help him leave; they cannot afford to. Emotional beat: the suffocating warmth of a community that needs you dead.

chapters.title: Ambrose's Confession
chapters.summary: Ambrose's POV. Ambrose was the generation's chosen one who fled in 1974 and has been dying slowly ever since, kept alive at the Well's threshold as a warning. He begs Zephyrine not to repeat his mistake. Emotional beat: pity for a man who is both victim and warden.

chapters.title: The Count Reaches Four
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile's counting drops to four. Her hair grays at the temples overnight. Zephyrine finds the ledger updating itself in wet ink. Emotional beat: time made visible, and a daughter becoming a stranger to herself.

chapters.title: What Zephyrine Buried
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He finally admits why he left home at seventeen: he heard the counting as a boy and ran, letting his younger brother be chosen in his place. The Well has never forgotten a debt. Emotional beat: self-deception collapsing into shame.

chapters.title: The Priest's Heresy
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The defrocked village priest shows him records from 1911: the bell wasn't melted, it was fed to the Well, and it rings from below whenever the covenant nears renewal. There may be a way to starve it. Emotional beat: a splinter of hope that costs information he can't unlearn.

chapters.title: Starving the Well
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Zephyrine and Ambrose seal the shaft, salt the foundations, and burn the ledger. The village's lights flicker; crops wilt within hours. Odile's counting pauses at three, then climbs back to five. Emotional beat: triumph that feels suspiciously like a trap being sprung.

chapters.title: The Village Rises
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The villagers, aging decades in days, surround the house with lanterns and quiet fury. They don't attack; they simply wait, because the Well is patient and so are they. Emotional beat: siege as social horror, the belonging he craved turned to a noose.

chapters.title: Ambrose Pays
chapters.summary: Ambrose's POV. Ambrose walks into the shaft at dawn, unsealing it himself, buying the family one week. His last words: 'It doesn't want a body, Zephyrine. It wants the one who ran twice.' Emotional beat: sacrifice that clarifies rather than resolves.

chapters.title: The Bell Rings Nine Times
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The bell tolls nine times; Odile's counting stops entirely, and she wakes lucid but hollow-eyed, saying the Well spoke to her in her father's voice. Emotional beat: the enemy stops being abstract and starts wearing familiar faces.

chapters.title: The Choice on the Ninth Floor
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Zephyrine descends alone. At the shaft's mouth the Well offers him the bargain it always intended: his life freely given, the debt of two generations erased, Odile freed. He hears his wife's voice, his brother's, his grandmother's, all counting down to one. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal and personal.

chapters.title: What Zephyrine Gave
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, fragmenting. He steps in, but not as a victim: he recites the ledger backwards, unpaying himself, offering the Well its own history as food. The shaft drinks the covenant instead of the man. The bell, far below, cracks. Emotional beat: sacrifice transfigured into defiance.

chapters.title: The House With Eight Floors
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile and Zephyrine, changed and half-deaf, walk out of Vellacourt as the village ages into dust behind them. The ninth floor is simply gone; the house has always had eight floors, the neighbors will say. Emotional beat: grief and release entangled, survival that no longer feels free.

chapters.title: The Dying Count Forwards Now
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, years later. Working hospice again in a distant city, Zephyrine hears the dying count, but now they count upwards, from one to nine, and stop. On the ninth number, they smile. He keeps a wax earplug in his pocket and never uses it. Emotional beat: uneasy peace, the belonging he found being the kind you carry alone.
